package fixture

import "testing"

// TestAssertPos has a run of six assertions: t.Errorf, t.Errorf, an if that
// only calls t.Fatal, assert.Equal, require.NoError, t.Error. t.Log breaks
// nothing because it comes after the run.
func TestAssertPos(t *testing.T) {
	got := compute()
	t.Errorf("a")
	// comments inside a run do not break it
	t.Errorf("b")
	if got != 1 {
		t.Fatal("c")
	}
	assert.Equal(t, 1, 1)
	require.NoError(t, nil)
	t.Error("f")
	t.Log("not an assertion")
}

// TestAssertNeg has two runs of five: the longest is 5.
func TestAssertNeg(t *testing.T) {
	t.Errorf("a")
	t.Errorf("b")
	t.Errorf("c")
	t.Errorf("d")
	t.Errorf("e")
	t.Log("break")
	t.Errorf("a")
	t.Errorf("b")
	t.Errorf("c")
	t.Errorf("d")
	t.Errorf("e")
}

// assertHelper is not a test: its assertions are not measured.
func assertHelper(t *testing.T) {
	t.Errorf("a")
}

// TestDupA and TestDupB share four identical assertions.
func TestDupA(t *testing.T) {
	setupA()
	assert.Equal(t, 1, got.A)
	assert.Equal(t, 2, got.B)
	assert.Equal(t, 3, got.C)
	assert.Equal(t, 4, got.D)
}

func TestDupB(t *testing.T) {
	setupB()
	assert.Equal(t, 1, got.A)
	assert.Equal(t, 2, got.B)
	assert.Equal(t, 3, got.C)
	assert.Equal(t, 4, got.D)
	check()
}

// TestNearA and TestNearB share only three identical assertions.
func TestNearA(t *testing.T) {
	assert.Equal(t, 1, want.A)
	assert.Equal(t, 2, want.B)
	assert.Equal(t, 3, want.C)
	assert.Equal(t, 4, want.D)
}

func TestNearB(t *testing.T) {
	assert.Equal(t, 1, want.A)
	assert.Equal(t, 2, want.B)
	assert.Equal(t, 3, want.C)
	assert.Equal(t, 5, want.E)
}

// TestSubtests: the t.Run closure is anonymous and counts toward the test.
func TestSubtests(t *testing.T) {
	t.Run("one", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Errorf("a")
		t.Errorf("b")
		t.Errorf("c")
	})
}

func BenchmarkSomething(b *testing.B) {}

func TestMain(m *testing.M) {}
